players.note: Since Week 5, Ollie Gordon has been the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 20 touches and 80.1 total yards. Among 45 qualifying backs this season, he is tenth in explosive run rate and 21st in missed tackle rate. Gordon should produce another solid volume-based RB2 stat line again this week. Over their last five games, Indy has allowed the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 11th-highest yards after contact per attempt.

Chase Brown is the RB20 in fantasy points per game as a weekly volume play. He has had horrible touchdown luck, with zero touchdowns since Week 1 and only one score this season. Since Week 5, Brown has averaged 15.8 touches and 73.5 total yards while splitting the early-down work with Samaje Perine. Since Week 5, Brown has had a 66.9% snap rate, a 47.9% rushing share, a 60% route share, and a 15.1% target share. Across his last three games, Brown's efficiency has begun to improve as Cincy's offensive line has gotten their act together. In those games, Brown has had 2.38 yards before contact per attempt, which has allowed him to rip a 13.3% explosive run rate and 2.38 yards after contact per attempt. Just for context, with that small 32-carry sample size. If Brown puts that sample up against all backs with at least 32 carries this season (62 rushers), he'd rank 15th in explosive run rate and 19th in yards after contact per attempt. Brown faces a tough matchup this week, but he should see enough volume to be at least a decent RB2. Over their last five games, the Steelers have allowed the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the third-lowest rushing success rate, and the fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Tetairoa McMillan is the WR14 in fantasy points per game, but since Week 7, with Bryce Young's struggles, he has been the WR28 in fantasy points per game. Overall, McMillan has a 21.7% target share with 2.08 YPRR, seven red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 30% first-read share. Since Week 7, his target share has dipped to 20.7% with 1.47 YPRR and a 28.6% first-read share. While McMIllan's production has fallen off with Young struggling, the decline hasn't been as steep as Jalen Coker has experienced. This passing attack could see a mini renaissance this week, though, against the Saints. New Orleans has the second-highest single-high rate (64.4%). Against single high, McMillan has a 23% TPRR with 1.95 YPRR. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the 14th-most receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, in his return, Breece Hall's workload was managed. He was second behind Braelon Allen in snap rate (43.5%) and route share (21.1%), while he led the duo in rushing workload (60% vs. 32%). Hall had a target or touch on 19 of his 27 snaps last week. Hall finished with 18 touches and 87 total yards. Hall had two red zone rushing attempts to Braelon Allen's one. The Jets eased Hall in, and I expect him to take over more of the snaps this week. Hall has posted only 1.68 yards after contact per attempt and a 15% missed tackle rate this season. Hall has another meh matchup this week. He could be a volume-based RB2 this week. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the 13th-lowest rushing success rate and the 11th-lowest yards after contact per attempt while ranking 15th in rushing yards over expectation per attempt and explosive run rate.

Since Week 5, Nico Collins' stranglehold on the top chair in the receiving room has slipped. In his last four games, he has had a 14.3% target share with 1.69 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and only a 20.7% first-read share. Collins has been the WR45 in fantasy points per game during this span. He's no longer a weekly must-start option. This week, he'll face a Browns' secondary that has the highest single-high rate in the NFL (73.6%). Since Week 5, against single-high, Collins has had only an 18% TPRR against single high but he has also produced 2.13 YPRR. Collins could be in trouble this week. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per attempt and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Rashee Rice is the WR36 in fantasy points per game. Over the last two games, he has returned to his low aDOT ways (2.47) with a 20.8% target share, 2.00 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 22.6% first-read share. Rice has had a 40% designed target rate in these two games. The PPR scam artist has returned. In these two outings, his slot rate has also bumped to 54.9%. Rice should post a solid stat line this week. Over their last five games, Atlanta has faced the eighth-fewest slot targets while ranking 16th in yards per target allowed to the position.

Garrett Wilson should be back this week (concussion). In his two games with Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. in the huddle, Garrett Wilson has had a 24.2% target share with 1.79 YPRR, three red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 26.5% first-read share. I expect him to lead the Jets' passing attack this week. Christian Benford has shadowed only twice this season and none since Week 2, so I'm not expecting that to happen this week. Wilson should eat this week as the Jets attempt to keep pace with the Bills' high-octane offense. Over their last five games, Buffalo has struggled with perimeter wide receivers, giving up the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Since Week 6, Tony Pollard has been the RB2 in fantasy points per game, averaging 23.7 touches and 122.6 total yards. Among 45 qualifying rushers, Pollard is 17th in explosive run rate, fifth in yards after contact per attempt, and 20th in missed tackle rate. He will face a formidable and new-look Jags run defense this week with the additions of Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Pollard will need all the volume he can swallow up this week. The Jags remain an elite run defense. Over their last five games, they have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Overall, Jalen Coker is the WR27 in fantasy points per game, but since Week 7, with Bryce Young's struggles, Coker has been the WR69 in fantasy points per game. Young's issues have impacted Coker more than Tetairoa McMillan. Since Week 7, Coker has had a 10.8% target share with 0.73 YPRR and a 19.6% first-read share. Overall, he has a 16.5% target share with 1.79 YPRR, seven red zone targets, ten deep targets, and a 24.8% first-read share. Coker could see a spike in production this week with the Saints' secondary on the menu. New Orleans has the second-highest single-high rate (64.4%). Against single-high, Coker has a 23% TPRR (tied with McMillan for the team lead) with a team-leading 2.22 YPRR. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the 14th-most receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, Zach Charbonnet took over as Seattle's lead back. He had a 57.4% snap rate, a 48.5% rushing share, and a 44.8% route share (7.1% target share). Charbonnet was the RB22 in weekly scoring with 17 touches and 86 total yards. In his limited action this season, Charbonnet has been impressive with 3.14 yards after contact per attempt and a 27% missed tackle rate. He should have plenty of room to rumble this week. Over their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, the 13th-most yards after contact per attempt, and the eighth-highest missed tackle rate.

George Pickens should crush this week. Pickens is the WR24 in fantasy points per game this season. He has a 19.5% target share with 2.00 YPRR, six red zone targets, ten deep targets, and a 22.7% first-read share. Pickens has been VERY coverage-sensitive this season, but the good news is this matchup lines up perfectly for him. Since Week 6, the 49ers have utilized single-high at the second-highest rate in the NFL (67.5%). Against single-high, Pickens has had a 33% TPRR and 2.66 YPRR. Over their last five games, the 49ers have ranked 16th in receiving fantasy points per game allowed to perimeter wide receivers while allowing the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Woody Marks has been posting hollow bell cow volume. Since Week 6, he has had a 76.5% snap rate, 66.7% of the rushing work, and a 54.3% route share (7.1% target share). During that span, he has averaged 18.6 touches with 78.7 total yards as the RB39 in fantasy points per game. The big problem continues to be his lack of touchdowns, as he has zero during that stretch. Among 45 qualifying rushers, he is 20th in explosive run rate and 23rd in missed tackle rate. Is this the Woody Marks breakout week? We shall see, but he has a wonderful matchup this week. David Montgomery's possible return could also toss a wrench into the gears for Marks. If Montgomery plays this week, I'm still projecting Marks to lead the backfield, but it would impact his previous bell cow usage. Over their last five games, the Browns' run defense continues to stink, allowing the second-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the second-highest missed tackle rate. Marks is an RB2/3 if Montgomery is active. If Montgomery is out, Marks is a volume-driven RB2.

Jameson Williams had a stinker game last week, but since Week 4 he has still been the WR14 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 4, Williams has had a 17.6% target share with 2.30 YPRR, seven red zone targets, ten deep targets, and a 25% first-read share. Williams should have a strong bounce-back game this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the second-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. The only thing that could derail Williams from smashing this week would be a Christian Gonzalez shadow, but Gonzalez got cooked last week by the Packers. I'm not downgrading Williams even with a possible shadow this week. Gonzalez has allowed two receivers to surpass 100 receiving yards in his shadow coverage this season (JSN & Matthew Golden).

Last week, DJ Moore wasn't a full-time player for Buffalo. He had a 66.7% route share, a 16.1% target share with 25 receiving yards (1.04 YPRR), and a 22.7% first-read share. The shoulder injury continues to linger despite being on the field now. In his four "full" games this season, Moore has had a 24.2% target share with 2.71 YPRR, four red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 25% first-read share. He is Buffalo's unquestioned WR1. He had a horrible matchup last week, but he could bounce back this week against the Jets' softer secondary. Over their last five games, New York has ranked 15th in yards per target while allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, Ashton Jeanty took back the lead back duties with a 66% snap rate, 40% of the rushing work, and a 62.5% route share. Jeanty finished with 11 touches and 20 total yards. The Raiders' offensive line has been a limited factor for Jeanty and this ground game all season. The Raiders' offensive line remains dead last in yards before contact per attempt. Jeanty has managed only 2.18 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate this season. Jeanty is only a low-end RB2/flex this week. Seattle remains a top-tier run defense. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the third-lowest explosive run rate, the third-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the eighth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Cam Skattebo will be back this week (hamstring). He practiced in full on Tuesday and Wednesday. He doesn't carry an injury designation into Week 10. The last time we saw Skattebo, he was racking up 18 touches and 121 total yards against the Texans as the RB7 for the week. In that game, he had a 55.4% snap rate, 50% of the rushing work, and a 32.3% route share. I expect him to see a similar workload (if not elevated) this week. Among 45 qualifying backs, Skattebo is 17th in yards after contact per attempt and 11th in missed tackle rate. Skattebo is a volume-based RB2 this week with a tough matchup. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Denzel Boston is the WR32 in fantasy points per game. He has a 20.6% target share with 1.70 YPRR, nine red zone targets, 16 deep targets, and a 24.7% first-read share. Boston had a nice outing against the Saints as the WR17 for the week. This week, he'll face another secondary that loves single-high. The Texans have the seventh-highest single-high rate (58.8%). Against single-high, Boston has had only a 15% TPRR with 0.63 YPRR. The coverage structure isn't in his favor. Houston has been allowing production to perimeter wide receivers, so maybe that helps save his day. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the tenth-most yards per target to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed. Boston didn't practice until Friday of this week. He did manage a limited practice session on Friday (toe). He has been listed as questionable. Monitor the news Sunday morning and have a backup plan in case he is ruled out.

DK Metcalf is headed for a long day in Week 10. He'll likely see shadow coverage from DJ Turner again. Metcalf is the WR43 in fantasy points per game, with three games this season with at least 12 PPR points. The last time he tangled with DJ Turner, he was shadowed on 77.1% of his routes, securing three of his five targets in his coverage with a score. That touchdown only occurred because Turner ran into another Cincy player, which left Metcalf wide open. Last year, in their two meetings, Turner followed Metcalf on 78.1-90.3% of his routes, holding him to 50 or fewer receiving yards in both games (zero scores). Overall, Metcalf has a 22.1% target share with 1.31 YPRR, five red zone targets, 15 deep targets, and a 31.4% first-read share. Sit Metcalf this week.

KC Concepcion had a strong game last week, as I projected. He was the WR10 for the week. That was his second game of the season with at least 18 PPR points. Concepcion has an 18.1% target share with 1.66 YPRR, three red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 25.8% first-read share (leads the team). The Texans have the seventh-highest single high rate (58.8%). Against single-high, Concepcion leads the team with a 22% TPRR and 2.01 YPRR. Concepcion is a strong flex again this week. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers while ranking 19th in fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Sam LaPorta didn't do much last week with a wonderful matchup. Over his last three games, he has had a 73.9% route share with only a 13.3% target share, 1.22 YPRR, two red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 12.2% first-read share. It's been shocking how little he has been utilized. LaPorta looks like he's headed for another down game this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per target and the ninth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 5, Blake Corum has been the RB16 in fantasy points per game, averaging 11.8 touches and 72.8 total yards. He has scored a touchdown in each game, which has helped to prop up the limited volume and hyper-efficiency. Among 45 qualifying backs, Corum is fourth in explosive run rate and 14th in missed tackle rate. Corum could see his hot streak come to an end this week, but the Rams could feed him more volume this week as Kyren Williams and Corum could be the engines of the offense. Over their last five games, Arizona's run defense has tightened up, allowing the ninth-lowest explosive run rate, the 12th-lowest rushing success rate, and ranking 15th in yards before contact per attempt.

Stefon Diggs is the WR25 in fantasy points per game with a 19.9% target share, 1.63 YPRR, six red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 24.1% first-read share. Without Terry McLaurin in the lineup, Diggs has had a 17.2% target share with 1.71 YPRR and a 20.8% first-read share. He's a volume-based flex this week who will need a score to pay off. The Giants have been shutting down slot receivers. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Since Week 5, Germie Bernard has been the WR23 in fantasy points per game. He should be busy this week, with DJ Turner following DK Metcalf. Since Week 5, Bernard has had a 22.2% target share with 1.85 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 22% first-read share. Over their last five games, Cincy has been destroyed by slot receivers, allowing the seventh-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Harold Fannin Jr. is the TE8 in fantasy points per game. He has a 17.7% target share with 1.68 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and an 18.1% first-read share. Fannin is a sit this week. Houston has been amazing against tight ends. Over their last five games, they have held the position to the second-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity. Consider streaming a tight end this week instead of playing Fannin.

Since Week 6, DeMario Douglas has been the WR17 in fantasy points per game. In those four games, he has had a 75.5% route share, a 19.4% target share, 2.66 YPRR, one red zone target, four deep targets, and a 20.5% first-read share. Douglas is a strong flex again this week. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the 14th-most yards per target and the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers.

Jakobi Meyers is the WR48 in fantasy points per game with four games of at least 10.5 PPR points. Meyers is in the flex conversation again this week. He has a 15.9% target share with 2.02 YPRR, eight red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 19% first-read share. Over their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the most receiving fantasy points per game and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, Dalton Kincaid saw his snap rate and route share tumble as the Bills trotted out Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes more, given their need to protect Josh Allen and run the ball. Dalton Kincaid had only a 50.6% snap rate and 47.2% route share. Kincaid's route share has dipped below 60% in three of his last five games. His usage is still fickle this season as it depends upon the matchups and Buffalo's game plan. When he has been on the field, Kincaid has still commanded targets with a 24% TPRR with 2.66 YPRR, six red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 20.3% first-read share. Kincaid's range of outcomes is wide again this week. The Jets have been bleeding out production to tight ends, but over their last five games they also have the fourth-best pressure rate. Kincaid could be heavily utilized this week or nerfed with a 40-50% route share. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Rhamondre Stevenson playing this week would severely impact Corey Kiner's workload. If Stevenson plays, I expect Kiner to factor in on early downs while Stevenson takes the passing-down work. If Stevenson is out, Kiner should be the rushing component of a split backfield with Lan Larison handling passing downs. Last week, in the fourth quarter, Kiner played 52.9% of the snaps with 87.5% of the rushing work, and zero routes. During this quarter, Lan Larison was also involved, but he only had one route with a 47.1% snap rate (one carry). Kiner has been impressive with his limited touches, with a 14.9% explosive run rate, 2.48 yards after contact per attempt, and a 30% missed tackle rate. Detroit's run defense has been nasty lately. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-lowest rushing success rate, the tenth-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the second-lowest yards after contact per attempt.

Since Week 6, Rachaad White has been the RB25 in fantasy points per game, averaging 11 touches and 62 total yards. In those games, he has had a 57.4% snap rate, 40.3% of the rushing work, and a 40.2% route share (10.6% target share). Among 45 qualifying rushers, White is 32nd in yards after contact per attempt and 13th in missed tackle rate. White is a volume-based RB2/3 this week against an improved Giants' run defense. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the ninth-lowest rushing success rate, the 13th-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the second-lowest missed tackle rate.

Quinshon Judkins is the RB25 in fantasy points per game, but he has been losing work to Dylan Sampson since Week 7. Over his last three games, he has averaged 15.6 touches and 66 total yards with a 42% snap rate, 55.1% of the rushing work, and a 16% route share. He has been primarily the early-down grinder, with Sampson handling passing downs and eating into his carry share. Judkins also continues to be inefficient with his rushing work. Among 45 qualifying rushers, he is 37th in explosive run rate, 39th in yards after contact per attempt, and 34th in missed tackle rate. Judkins could see a bump in these numbers this week. Houston's run defense has softened some recently. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the third-highest rushing success rate, the ninth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate. With his lack of passing game involvement, Judkins still likely needs a touchdown to pay off in fantasy this week.

In his last two games, with Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell on the field, Omar Cooper has had an 8.1% target share with 2.40 YPRR, one red zone target, two deep targets, and a 10.2% first-read share. Those are sleepy numbers for the talented rookie. Unfortunately, it looks like he's headed for a quiet week. Over their last five games, Buffalo has held slot receivers to the third-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, as he played through a foot injury, Hunter Henry had only a 50.8% snap rate, a 47.8% route share, a 7.3% target share, and a 10% first-read share. Hunter Henry managed limited practices all week. He doesn't have an injury designation this week, but that doesn't really mean anything to me. The Pats have talented rookie Eli Raridon who can take some of the lifting this week off Henry's plate as he plays through this foot injury. Henry could see a bump in his routes this week, making him a smash play, but I also won't be shocked if he is a part-time player again in Week 10. Overall, Henry has had a 12.8% target share with 1.89 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 14.3% first-read share. Henry has three TE1 finishes this season in weekly scoring (TE10, TE7, TE8). Henry is the TE21 in fantasy points per game. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the second-most receiving fantasy points per game and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Henry could be a TE1 this week.

Since Week 4, Tucker Kraft has been the TE7 in fantasy points per game. He has had a 16.1% target share with 1.53 YPRR, eight red zone targets, four deep targets, and an 18.2% first-read share. Kraft will need a score to return TE1-level fantasy production this week. He has a horrible matchup. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Caleb Douglas is the WR28 in fantasy points per game, but we'll see if his production takes a hit this week with Kyle McCord under center. Douglas has had at least 70 receiving yards in three of his five games played this season. Douglas has a 19.4% target share with 2.45 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 26.5% first-read share. Over their last five games, Indy has ranked 15th in yards per target while allowing the 14th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. Douglas is a middle-of-the-road flex this week with a sizable amount of risk.

Last week, Jordyn Tyson was eased back in with his first regular-season action after being sidelined with hamstring issues. Tyson had a 23.6% snap rate, a 33.3% route share, a 27% TPRR (11.4% target share), 2.00 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 14.3% first-read share. I expect the Saints to slowly ramp up their talented rookie. I wouldn't be surprised to see him log a 40% snap rate and 50-60% route share this week, but it's an in-the-dark projection. I don't want to start Tyson this week, but he does have a nice matchup. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the third-most receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Deebo Samuel will be back this week (hamstring). Samuel has two top-20 weeks in weekly fantasy scoring this season (WR13, WR20). Samuel has a 12.7% target share with 2.12 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 14.4% first-read share in his five games played. Samuel is a low-end flex this week. Over their last five games, Dallas has ranked 16th in yards per target against slot receivers while allowing the fifth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Last week, Alvin Kamara didn't see his role grow as he operated as the passing-down back almost exclusively. Kamara had a 48.6% snap rate with only 18.8% of the rushing work, a 57.8% route share, and an 11.4% target share. Kamara finished with nine touches and 49 total yards (zero touchdowns). Kamara is only a middling PPR flex this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and the 14th-fewest receiving fantasy points per game to backs.

With Bam Knight back, Tyler Allgeier will split the work with him this week. In Weeks 6 & 7, Allgeier had a 51% snap rate, 44.1% of the rushing work, and a 39.8% route share (4.8% target share). Allgeier averaged 15 touches and 48.5 total yards. Allgeier hasn't been efficient with his workload this season, with only a 7.3% explosive run rate and a 10% missed tackle rate. He's a middling flex this week with a bad matchup. The Rams' run defense has been improving. In their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, the seventh-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the sixth-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Jordan Addison is the WR65 in fantasy points per game with only two games this season with double-digit PPR points, but with the arrival of Kirk Cousins, hopefully, better days could be ahead. Addison has a 17.9% target share with 1.34 YPRR, one red zone target, nine deep targets, and a 25% first-read share. Across their last five games, Green Bay has allowed the ninth-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Sit Addison this week.

Since Week 5, Kyle Pitts has been the TE6 in fantasy points per game, but he has turned in stinkers in each of the last two games with a combined 7.9 PPR points. An issue in those games that isn't going away is Michael Penix's poor play. In those games, Pitts had an 18.2% target share and 25% first-read share, but only 50% of his targets were deemed catchable. This explains his 29 receiving yards and 0.63 YPRR. We'll see if Pitts can bounce back this week. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the third-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends. I want to be hopeful, but I just saw Penix crush Pitts against Cincy, who has been unable to stop tight ends all season.

Since Week 3, Ryan Flournoy has had three top-24 finishes in weekly scoring (WR15, WR23, WR23). During that span, Flournoy has had a 12.9% target share with 1.54 YPRR, eight red zone targets, three deep targets, and an 11.7% first-read share. Since Week 6, the 49ers have utilized single-high at the second-highest rate in the NFL (67.5%). Since Week 3, against single-high, Flournoy has had only a 12% TPRR, but he has also had 1.88 YPRR. He has been productive with his opportunities, but this isn't the matchup to consider flexing him. Over their last five games, the 49ers have held slot receivers to the tenth-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, Audric Estime took over the "Kendre Miller role" in the Saints offense as the primary early down thumper. Estime had a 48.6% snap rate, 46.9% of the rushing work, and a 28.9% route share (2.9% target share). Estime handled all three of the red zone rushing attempts as he scored a touchdown. Estime was the RB10 for the week as he finished with 16 touches and 77 total yards. Estime has 2.08 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Estime is a solid flex again this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the 14th-highest rushing success rate, the eighth-highest yards before contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 4, Khalil Shakir has been the WR32 in fantasy points per game. During this stretch, Shakir has had a 17.3% target share with 2.56 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 20.4% first-read share. This week, he's a middling PPR flex. Over their last five games, the Jets have ranked 16th in yards per target and 17th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to slot receivers.

Wan'Dale Robinson is the WR43 in fantasy points per game with four games of at least 11 PPR points this season. He excelled in Week 8 with a soft matchup against Cincy as the WR15 for the week. Robinson has a 19.8% target share with 1.19 YPRR, ten red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 24.9% first-read share. Robinson is only a low-end PPR flex this week. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the eighth-fewest yards per target and the ninth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers.

Brenton Strange has been awesome on a per-route basis, but the fact that the Jags have been blowing out teams has limited his production as the TE19 in fantasy points per game. Strange has a 66.3% route share with a 16.2% target share, 2.16 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 17.7% first-read share. Among 41 qualifying tight ends, he is 11th in fantasy points per route run. Strange could be a TE1 this week. Over their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the 13th-most yards per target and the eighth-mos fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.
Ladd McConkey missed last week's game with back spasms. I'll update his outlook on Saturday, but he could be back in the huddle this week.

Last week, Tank Dell blew up as the WR8 for the week. Dell had a 47% snap rate and 55% route share while seeing a wonderful 24.3% target share and 39.1% first-read share. Dell produced 105 receiving yards (4.77 YPRR) while seeing one red zone target and four deep targets. This week, I expect his snap count to grow some, but he has a tough matchup incoming. This week, he'll face a Browns' secondary that has the highest single-high rate in the NFL (73.6%). In his two games of action against single-high, he has had a 55% TPRR and 3.55 YPRR, but it's only an 11-route sample, so take it with a grain of salt. Dell could produce this week, but it's not an easy matchup. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per attempt and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. He's a dice-roll flex play this week.

In the last two games with Garrett Wilson available and Omar Cooper Jr. assimilated into the offense, Adonai Mitchell has had a 19.4% target share with 3.38 YPRR, two red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 24.5% first-read share. During those games, Mitchell has remained the team's field stretcher with a 20.6 aDOT and 50% of his target volume coming via deep targets. The Bills have been vulnerable to perimeter wide receivers in recent weeks, but they have done an excellent job defending downfield passing. This dichotomy creates a wide range of outcomes for Mitchell's Week 10 outlook. Over their last five games, Buffalo has struggled with perimeter wide receivers, giving up the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. During that span, they have also limited opposing offenses to the tenth-lowest passing success rate and the seventh-fewest deep passing yards. If Mitchell can connect on one or two deep targets this week, it could make his fantasy day, but the chances of that happening look slim. He's a very risky but high-upside flex.

Since Week 7, Rico Dowdle has been the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15 touches and 71 total yards. In those two games, Dowdle has had a 45.9% snap rate, a 38.1% rushing share, and a 45% route share (10.9% target share). Among 51 qualifying backs, Dowdle is 11th in yards after contact per attempt and 29th in missed tackle rate. Dowdle is a strong flex at his floor, but he could easily be an RB2 again this week. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the fourth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-highest yards after contact per attempt.

Since Week 7, Chig Okonkwo has been the TE25 in fantasy points per game, with one outing with double-digit PPR points. He has had a 17.2% target share with 1.51 YPRR, one red zone target, and an 18.8% first-read share. Sit Okonkwo this week. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the third-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 5, Tyler Higbee has led the tight end room with a 76.8% snap rate, a 65.6% route share, a 10.3% target share, and a 12.8% first-read share. Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen have combined for nine red zone targets during this stretch of games, and Hibee has only one. I could say he's due, but it's also clear the Rams' preference has been to use Parkinson and Allen in the red zone more. Over their last five games, Arizona has faced the fourth-fewest tight end targets, but they are allowing the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Higbee is on the streaming radar this week.

The Bengals have been a wonderful matchup for tight ends this season, but I'm projecting another down game for Pat Freiermuth this week. The last time he faced Cincy, he secured two of his four targets with 30 scoreless receiving yards. This all goes back to the coverage structure for Cincy. The last time they played Pittsburgh, they utilized single high with 59.5% of their defensive snaps. In three of their last four games, they have utilized single high 52.5-67.4% of their defensive snaps. Freiermuth disappears against single high with a 13% TPRR and 0.98 YPRR. Sit Freiermuth this week.

Since Jordan Mason's return, Aaron Jones has taken a step back with a 32.9% snap rate, a 30.5% rushing share, and a 22.9% route share. He has averaged only 7.3 touches and 29 total yards. Unless his role changes this week, this will be the last week that Jones is a must-write-up for the Primer, as he is just a change of pace/back up option for Minnesota right now. Jones is a low-end flex option this week, though. Over their last five games, Green Bay has allowed the 13th-highest rushing success rate, the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

Overall, Darren Waller is the TE16 in fantasy points per game with two TE1 finishes in weekly scoring (TE5, TE1). Waller has managed four games with double-digit PPR points. Last week, Waller saw a huge spike in his usage with a season-high 67.4% route share, 25.6% target share, and 28.6% first-read share. I don't expect that usage to continue this week, but considering how good Waller was last week, it might be tough for Carolina to put that genie back in the bottle. Overall, Waller has a 54.3% route share, a 9.6% target share, 1.58 YPRR, four red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 10.6% first-read share. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Over the last three games, Jordan Mason has taken over as Minny's lead back with a 46.7% snap rate, a 49.2% rushing share, and a 29.2% route share (5.9% target share). He has averaged 10.4 touches and 43.3 total yards. Mason has a strong 14.3% explosive run rate and a decent 2.02 yards after contact per attempt. He could return low-end RB2/solid flex numbers this week. Over their last five games, Green Bay has allowed the 13th-highest rushing success rate, the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Braelon Allen led the Jets' backfield in snap rate (58.1%) while seeing only a 32% rushing share, but he led the backfield in route share (39.5%). Allen was behind Breece Hall in opportunities, though. Allen finished with ten touches and 54 total yards. Hall had two red zone rushing attempts to Braelon Allen's one. Allen could see his workload take a step back this week with Hall another week away from his original injury. Allen is an RB3 who could post flex production if he gets in the end zone. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the 13th-lowest rushing success rate and the 11th-lowest yards after contact per attempt while ranking 15th in rushing yards over expectation per attempt and explosive run rate.

Since Week 7, Dylan Sampson has had a 55.5% snap rate, 19.2% of the rushing work, and a 52.7% route share (11.1% target share). Sampson has averaged nine touches and 64.3 total yards as the RB36 in fantasy points per game. Sampson has 2.13 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Neither of those marks are impressive. He can still be a decent flex this week in PPR formats. Over their last five games, Houston is tied for the most receiving touchdowns allowed to running backs while also surrendering the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game to the position.

We'll see how much Keenan Allen plays this week with a new playbook to pick up and a new quarterback to build rapport with on the fly. Allen is the WR37 in fantasy points per game this season, with four weeks as a top-36 wide receiver in weekly scoring. This season, Allen has earned a 21.5% target share with 1.74 YPRR, five red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 26.4% first-read share. Allen is a risky but could be profitable flex this week. Dallas continues to bleed out production to perimeter wide receivers. Over their last five games, they have allowed the ninth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the eighth-most fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Tre Tucker is the WR28 in fantasy points per game, but he'll take a hit this week with Fernando Mendoza making his first start against an elite pass defense. Tucker has a 17.3% target share with 2.06 YPRR, seven red zone targets, 11 deep targets, and a 22% first-read share. Over their last five games, Seattle has held perimeter receivers to the ninth-fewest yards per target while ranking 18th in fantasy points per opportunity. Tucker is a low-end flex this week.

Last week, Juwan Johnson was the TE10 for the week. Johnson had a 52.8% snap rate and 64.4% route share. That was his highest route share since Week 5. Johnson still only had a 5.7% target share and 9.5% first-read share. His touchdown fueled his fantasy day. Since Week 6, his role in the passing attack has shriveled up with only a 4.9% target share, 0.59 YPRR, and a 7.8% first-read share. Johnson is a sit until his role changes. Over their last five games, Carolina has held tight ends to the 12th-lowest yards per target and the 14th-fewest receiving fantasy points per game.

Mike Gesicki is the TE12 in fantasy points per game, but that is really just fueled by six touchdowns in eight games played. Over the last two games, his role has grown with a 69.4% route share, 10.4% target share, 1.47 YPRR, and a 13.5% first-read share. Gesicki is on the streaming radar again this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the third-most yards per target and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Dalton Schultz has become a part-time player in the Houston offense. Last week, he had only a 45.5% snap rate and 50% route share. He only managed an 8.1% target share and two receptions. Schultz is a sit until his role changes.

Josh Downs could make a major impact for the Chiefs moving forward, but he's a sit this week. I expect Downs to be a limited-snap player this week as he learns the playbook. The matchup is good, but his playing time is a big question mark for Week 10. Leave him on the bench this week.

Omarion Hampton is the RB44 in fantasy points per game, averaging 14.2 touches and 54 total yards. Hampton hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 4. He has a 43% snap rate, a 45.5% rushing workload, and a 22.2% route share. Hampton has managed only 2.24 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Hampton is a sit again this week. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the second-lowest explosive run rate, the eighth-lowest rushing success rate, and the sixth-lowest yards after contact per attempt.

Without Davante Adams in the lineup the last three games, the Rams have utilized 13 personnel (three tight end sets) with 47.2-54.8% of their offensive snaps. It has left Konata Mumpfield a part-time player. Last week, Konata Mumpfield had only a 42.5% snap rate and a 44.4% route share. In Weeks 2-3, with Davante Adams active and Nacua out, Mumpfield had a 71.8% snap rate, a 66.7% route share, an 11.6% target share with 1.69 YPRR, and an 11.7% first-read share. Mumpfield isn't a high-end target earner. I expect Mumpfield to be the primary receiver with all the tight ends this week as the full-time option, based on his ascension earlier in the season and his ability to help in the run-blocking department. That's not something the Rams should be asking Tutu Atwell to do often. The Cardinals have the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (65.5%). In Weeks 2-3, against two-high, Mumpfield saw his target-per-route run rate jump from 14% to 20% and his YPRR jump from 0.97 to 2.76. Now, this is only a 62-route sample, but it's worth noting. Over the last five games, Arizona has allowed the 14th-most yards per target to perimeter wide receivers. Zoom out to the entire season, and they have allowed the third-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Mumpfield is a decent flex this week with a wonderful matchup. My biggest concerns for Mumpfield are his ability to earn a higher target share and Matthew Stafford's passing volume.

AJ Brown (knee/ankle) was limited in practice all week and has been listed as questionable. The reports sound hopeful that he will suit up this week. I can't say that I have a ton of trust in AJ Brown at this point, even if he plays. This season, when Brown has been on the field, he hasn't been good, and I know that is because of health, but he still isn't 100% this week. In Weeks 6 and 7, he was the WR60 and WR35 in weekly scoring. Brown had a 23.8% target share and 39.5% first-read share in those games, but he only managed 75 receiving yards total (1.17 YPRR) while drawing three red zone targets and three deep targets. The Lions have been discussed as a wonderful matchup for Brown this week, but that isn't the case. Over their last five games, the Lions have allowed the third-fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. I'm wary of Brown this week, but I understand many fantasy GMs will have no choice but to plug him into a starting lineup. Just temper your expectations.

Last week, Xavier Hutchinson became Houston's starting slot receiver, running 65.6% of his routes from the slot. Hutchinson had an 80% route share (led the team) with a 13.5% target share, 0.91 YPRR, 29 receiving yards, one red zone target, a deep target, and a 21.7% first-read share (second on the team). Hutchinson is a sit this week. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

With Bam Knight back this week (concussion), the Cards will roll with a committee backfield this week. In Weeks 6 & 7, Knight had a 49% snap rate, 37.3% of the rushing work, and a 38.6% route share (8.4% target share). In those two games, he averaged 13.5 touches and 80.5 total yards. He has been quite good this season with his limited work, with 2.93 yards after contact per attempt and a 25% missed tackle rate. Knight is only a middling flex this week, though. The Rams' run defense has been improving. In their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, the seventh-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the sixth-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Emmett Johnson could turn in flex-worthy numbers this week. Over the last two games, he has gotten in the end zone in each game while averaging six touches and 88.5 total yards. Johnson has been incredible with his limited workload, with an astounding 3.27 yards after contact per attempt and a 35% missed tackle rate. The Falcons have had a Swiss cheese run defense. Over their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the seventh-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards after contact per attempt. Johnson could see 10-12 touches this week if Kansas City wants to lean on their ground game more with Patrick Mahomes playing through an injury.

In Drew Lock's two starts, AJ Barner has finished as the TE20 and TE5 in weekly scoring. With that higher finish, I also have to mention that he scored a rushing touchdown in that game. In those games, Barner had a 9.3% target share, 0.41 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 7.5% first-read share. Barner is a low-end streaming option this week. Over their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the sixth-most receiving fantasy points per game and ranked 19th in fantasy points per opportunity against tight ends.

Last week, Kaleb Johnson finished with 14 carries, 68 yards on the ground, and a score. I expect him to be the early-down option for Green Bay's committee backfield. Johnson has been awesome on a per-touch basis this season with 2.83 yards after contact per attempt and a 26% missed tackle rate. The Green Bay offensive line has only managed to generate 1.26 yards before contact per attempt for him, though. I don't expect that number to be higher this week, but if he can find a crease, he could do some damage against this Minny run defense. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate. Johnson could be a decent flex option this week.

Ok, we're going back to Darnell Washington this week as a streaming option. Yep, you guessed it. It's because of single-high coverage. The last time they played Pittsburgh, they utilized single high with 59.5% of their defensive snaps. In three of their last four games, they have utilized single high 52.5-67.4% of their defensive snaps. The last time Washington faced this defense, he secured three of his four targets with 67 receiving yards (zero touchdowns). Against single high, Washington has a 27% TPRR and 2.72 YPRR. With DK Metcalf dealing with DJ Turner all game, Washington could see a decent workload. Washington is tied for the team lead with seven red zone targets and has three scores this season. He could be a TE1 this week. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the tenth-most yards per target to tight ends while ranking 15th in receiving fantasy points per game.

Chris Rodriguez is a viable flex option again this week. Rodriguez has 12 red zone carries this season while averaging 7.4 touches and 33 total yards. If he gets into the end zone this week, he could give you a comfy double-digit PPR points. Rodriguez has posted 2.20 yards after contact per attempt and an 18% missed tackle rate this season. The Titans' run defense has been giving. Over their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, and the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt.

Over the last two games, Kaelon Black has averaged 11.5 rushing attempts and 66.5 rushing yards while logging a 35.3% snap rate. He could easily see 10-12 touches again this week as a decent flex play. Black is a touchdown-dependent flex. He has almost no passing game role with only six targets this season. Black has posted a solid 2.43 yards after contact per attempt and a 15% missed tackle rate. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 14th-highest explosive run rate, the second-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Tutu Atwell might only be a part-time player this week. I expect the Rams to lean on the run a ton. Since Week 7, Atwell has had only a 40.2% snap rate, a 52.5% route share, and a 9.3% target share. Konata Mumpfield is likely the full-time receiver, with the Rams' three tight ends on the field a ton.

Xavier Worthy is the WR57 in fantasy points per game, and now he'll have to contend with Josh Downs weekly for targets behind Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce. Worthy has a 17.9% target share with 1.17 YPRR, eight red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 24% first-read share. He's a low-end flex option this week. Over the last five games, Atlanta has allowed the ninth-most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.
If Ladd McConkey isn't available this week, I'll be writing up Tre Harris as a flex option this week, but we won't know that until this weekend. I'll update his outlook on Saturday.

Mark Andrews is the TE29 in fantasy points per game. Andrews hasn't managed double-digit PPR points since Week 4. Andrews has a 17.4% target share with 1.26 YPRR, seven red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 19.3% first-read share. Andrews is on the streaming radar this week. Yes, I'm assuming that many people have dropped him at this point in the season. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the most yards per target and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Ashton Dulin will assume a starting role this week after Indy's trades. This season, he has a 24% TPRR, 2.21 YPRR, and an 8.7% first-read share. Dulin is only interesting as a desperation flex this week because of how bad Miami has been against perimeter wide receivers and his small sample efficiency. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

MarShawn Lloyd missed last week's game with a knee issue. He opened this week not on the injury report. I expect Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson to split the backfield work this week, with Lloyd handling the passing downs more and chipping in on early downs. Lloyd has only 1.37 yards after contact per attempt and a 16% missed tackle rate this season. As a passing-down option, he has a 24.8% route share and 5.4% target share this season. None of this is incredibly appealing. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate, but the Packers don't have the offensive line talent to consistently open running lanes for their backs. Lloyd is a low-end flex option this week.

Brian Thomas remains off the fantasy radar. Since Week 5, he has had a 39.3% route share, a 5.7% target share, 0.23 YPRR, and a 7.6% first-read share. Unless his role changes this week, this will be the last time I worry about writing him up for the Primer.

Brevyn Spann-Ford should take over as Dallas's starting tight end this week with Jake Ferguson sidelined. This season, Spann-Ford has had a 20% TPRR, 1.33 YPRR, two red zone targets, and a 6.1% first-read share in limited duty. Last week, he had a 67.6% route share, a 17.2% target share, 1.24 YPRR (31 receiving yards), and a 23.5% first-read share. He's on the streaming radar this week. The 49ers, over their last five games, have allowed the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends while ranking 18th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed.

David Montgomery could be back this week. Montgomery opened the week with a DNP before upgrading to a limited session on Thursday and a full practice on Friday. I don't expect Montgomery to lead the backfield this week if he is back. I'd expect him to split the work with Woody Marks or play a change-of-pace role. Montgomery hasn't been efficient with his work this season, with a 2.1% explosive run rate, 1.65 yards after contact per attempt, and a 13% missed tackle rate. The matchup is glorious, though, and could help those sagging numbers. Over their last five games, the Browns' run defense continues to stink, allowing the second-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the second-highest missed tackle rate. If Montgomery is active, he's likely a touchdown-dependent flex this week.

Travis Etienne opened this week with limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday (hamstring). He upgraded to a full practice on Friday. I don't expect him to be back this week, but I'll update his outlook on Saturday.
